question: How accurately can Tubesense locate the train between stations without GPS?
norm_question: how accurately can tubesense locate the train between stations without gps

answer.text: Tubesense achieves a 1.8 m median error against yaw curve-edge truth across 10 forward-test rides (versus 11.2 m for a timetable baseline) and a 13.5 m median error across 19 hidden curve edges in leave-one-run-out evaluation (versus 22.8 m).

verified_claims.text: Across 10 forward-test Central line rides using frozen maps from the previous day, Tubesense achieved a chord-scaled median positioning error of 1.8 m against yaw curve-edge truth, compared with 11.2 m for a timetable baseline, and a mean coverage fraction of 0.951.
On the pre-registered forward test across 6 runs between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, the positioning verdict is GO, with a median error of 1.95 m and mean coverage of 0.963.

When yaw is hidden around each curve edge in a leave-one-run-out evaluation across 19 Central line curve edges over both days, Tubesense has a median between-curves error of 13.5 m, compared with 22.8 m for the timetable baseline at the same hidden curve edges.
In the post-hoc forward test across 10 runs, Tubesense achieved a median positioning error of 1.8 m, compared with 11.85 m for the timetable baseline, and a mean coverage fraction of 0.936.

In the post-hoc forward test across 10 runs using Working Timetable station distances, Tubesense achieved a median positioning error of 1.8 m, compared with 11.85 m for the timetable baseline, and a mean coverage fraction of 0.936.
